You will perform standard industrial applications found at a marine oil terminal such as installing, modifying, repairing, troubleshooting, testing, and loading new and existing electrical lines and circuits.
You will works from building plans, blueprints, wiring diagrams, engineering, drawings, and electrical maintenance and repair manuals to plan and lay out the routing, placement type, size, gauge, balance, etc.
You will use a wide variety of testing equipment, including test lamps, multimeters, circuit analyzers, circuit breaker testers, voltage recording meters, meggers, watt meters, ohmeters, and ammeters.
You will be required to perform general maintenance and repair duties on the facilities as required.
Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most trade and labor occupations, you must show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying.

Qualification requirements emphasis is on quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time. Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the job elements and screen out listed below.

This job has a screen-out element which will be used to determine minimum eligibility for this job. Applicants who do not receive a minimum of two points on the screen-out element(s) will be found ineligible.

The Screen-out Element for this position is: ABILITY TO DO THE WORK OF THE POSITION WITHOUT MORE THAN NORMAL SUPERVISION *Demonstrated knowledge in the installation, operation, and troubleshooting of various electrical systems and equipment, including series, parallel, and compound circuits for single and multiple-phase alternating currents; *Ability to interpret and apply the National Electrical Code, local codes, building plans, blueprints, and wiring diagrams to plan, lay out, and complete electrical work; *Proficient in using a wide variety of hand tools, power tools (like hydraulic benders and pipe threading machines), and specialized test equipment such as multimeters, meggers, circuit analyzers, and optical time domain reflectometers (OTDR); *Ability to install, modify, repair, and maintain diverse industrial and marine electrical systems, such as secondary power distribution lines, switchgear, fire alarm systems, lighting protection, and fiber optic networks; *Must be able to obtain and maintain a Forklift Operator License and a U.S.

Driver's License or government vehicle operator permit. Applicants must meet the requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Job Qualification Handbook for Trades and Labor Occupations.

Additional qualification information can be found at: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/federal-wage-system-qualifications/#url=List-of-Approved-Job-Elements Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

At Sunrun, we're on a mission to change the way the world interacts with energy, and we're building a company and brand that puts power at the center of life. To do it, we're designing a dynamic culture where employee development, well-being, and safety come first. It's why we've become the #1 home solar and battery company in America.

We're unlike any other residential energy company. Our vertically integrated model gives us total control over every part of the energy lifecycle - from sale through installation and beyond - so you can find endless opportunities for growth. Come join a career you can grow in and a culture you can run with.
Who We Are
We're on a mission to make energy more reliable and affordable for more people. We provide an opportunity with storage and solar to help people access greater energy independence without the big upfront costs. Sunrun is the largest dedicated residential solar and storage company in the country and has a mission to bring stably priced resilient power to the masses.

Help launch Sunrun's brand-new St. Louis branch! As America's #1 home solar and battery company, we are seeking an experienced Non-Certified Electrician to join our team starting now!
As a key member of our launch team, you will spend your first few months gaining hands-on leadership experience alongside our established Chicago team before permanently running installation crews out of our new St. Louis branch when doors open in early 2027.
Through our Power+ program, we invest heavily in your skills and career development, offering cross-training across solar, battery, and service operations to build long-term job security.

While supporting operations in Chicago during the pre-launch phase, Sunrun covers 100% of your travel overhead:
Rotation Schedule: 2 weeks on-site in Chicago, followed by 4 full days off at home in St. Louis.
Company Vehicle: Dedicated company vehicle provided for travel and work use.
Paid Travel Time: Full hourly compensation for time spent traveling between St. Louis and Chicago.
Lodging & Meal Allowance: 100% company-paid hotel accommodations plus daily per diem.

Electrical Installation & Interconnection: Lead or assist in the installation of electrical systems interconnecting residential solar arrays and battery storage systems to the power grid.
Service & Troubleshooting: Perform Main Panel Upgrades (MPUs), troubleshoot system issues, resolve electrical problems, and assist with necessary repairs or commissioning.
Crew Support & Leadership: Support the PV installation crew on-site and step up to lead the crew when the Foreperson is absent.
Code & Safety Compliance: Ensure work meets high workmanship standards, complies with current NEC and local codes, and strictly adheres to OSHA safety standards and Sunrun practices.
Inspections & Communication: Coordinate with local inspectors as assigned, and work closely with homeowners and branch teams to deliver a top-tier customer experience.

Education & Apprenticeship Hours: High school diploma or equivalent. Must possess 75% of the hours required to sit for state-specific electrical certification exams (Certified Electrical Trainee preferred or required depending on state regulations).
Electrical Experience: Hands-on electrical installation and repair experience, including work with wiring up to 600 VDC / 480 VAC. Working knowledge of replacing residential electrical services and distribution panels preferred.
Technical & Code Proficiency: Working knowledge of NEC codes, ability to interpret single-line drawings/PV system schematics from roof to meter, and solid understanding of solar interconnection principles and basic construction.
Driver Requirements: Must be at least 21 years old with a valid driver's license and a clean driving record (ability to pass a driving background check).
Soft Skills & Ownership: Strong troubleshooting and logical decision-making skills, customer focus, and a results-driven attitude with the ability to lead when necessary.
Physical Demands
Lifting & Transport: Ability to regularly transport materials and equipment up to 50 lbs (and up to 100 lbs with assistance).

At FEMA, our mission is to help people before, during and after disasters, and every employee at FEMA has a role in emergency management.

Every FEMA employee has regular and recurring emergency management responsibilities, though not every position requires routine deployment to disaster sites.

All positions are subject to recall around the clock for emergency management operations, which may require irregular work hours, work at locations other than the official duty station, and may include duties other than those specified in the employee's official position description.

Travel requirements in support of emergency operations may be extensive in nature (weeks to months), with little advance notice, and may require employees to relocate to emergency sites with physically austere and operationally challenging conditions.
The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of this announcement. Ability to Lead or Supervise Ability to supervise or lead electricians performing common tasks for low and high voltage electrical systems and equipment; plan, coordinate, and assign work to provide technical direction or help.

Able to install, modify, repair, maintain, troubleshoot, and test electrical lines, circuits, systems and equipment. Use working knowledge or ability under close supervision of a work leader using building plans, wiring diagrams, engineering drawings to plan and layout routing of electrical equipment.

Applicants will be rated in accordance with the OPM Federal Wage System Qualification Standard.

Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most trade and labor occupations, you must meet any screen-out element listed, and show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying.

Qualification requirements emphasis is on the quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time. Working Conditions: The work is performed both inside and outside.

Electrical workers are sometimes required to make repairs and installations in bad weather; in work areas that are noisy, dirty, dusty, and greasy; on scaffolding or cranes at heights of 9 meters (30 feet) or more; and in close quarters such as manholes, or attics.

They are occasionally exposed to the possibility of injury from falling, electrical shock, burns, and rotary devices such as electrical motors. They are frequently exposed to the possibility of cuts and bruises.

They are exposed to danger from explosions of equipment and cables in manholes and vaults, as well as danger from high voltage electrical shock, burns from solder, broken bones, cuts, and bruises.

They are exposed to heat and noise when working in substationsor power-generating facilities, to extremes of weather when working outdoors, and to unpleasant odors and wet slippery surfaces when working in manholes.

They are subject to electrical burns while working around high voltage electrical lines, broken bones fromfalls from poles, and strains from awkward work positions. They are exposed to chemicals such as insulation oil from transformers and oil switches. They use protective devices such as earplugs, safety hats, and nonconductive gloves and footwear.

Physical Effort: Workers frequently perform moderately heavy lifting, pulling, and carrying of equipment and material weighing up to 18 kilograms (40 pounds) and occasionally, they lift or pull heavy cables and equipment weighing more than 23 kilograms ( 50 pounds) with the help of weight handling equipment or with assistance from other workers.

They use block and tackle, pulleys, or other lifting devices. They crouch, stand, kneel, and stoop while installing, repairing, or testing electrical equipment in confined spaces such as enclosed switch gear, or in structures such as overhead bus and conduit assemblies.

Workers work above ground from aerial bucket trucks and poles, at ground level, and in trenches, or manholes. Work requires bending, stooping, climbing, and standing for long periods while installing, repairing, and testing electrical equipment in manholes and on overhead distribution lines in tiring and uncomfortable positions.

Electrical workers make repairs and installations from ladders, scaffolding, platforms, and other hard-to-reach places.

L'entreprise
Capner est une entreprise suisse de la transition énergétique. Depuis notre siège de Neuchâtel, nous installons des solutions solaires complètes : panneaux photovoltaïques, onduleurs et batteries, bornes de recharge, ... Objectif : rendre nos clients plus autonomes en énergie.
Nos chantiers se trouvent surtout dans le canton de Neuchâtel, du Littoral aux Montagnes (Neuchâtel, La Chaux\-de\-Fonds, Le Locle), et dans le canton de Vaud : région lausannoise, La Côte, Nord vaudois jusqu'à Yverdon\-les\-Bains.
Pour suivre le rythme, nous renforçons notre secteur courant alternatif (AC). La pose des panneaux en toiture est assurée par d'autres équipes. Vous, vous intervenez côté tableau électrique, au moment où l'installation prend vie : raccordement, mise en service, premiers kilowattheures produits.
Vous voulez un poste où votre CFC d'installateur\-électricien sert vraiment, sur des installations solaires récentes ? Lisez la suite.
Votre mission
* Raccorder les installations côté courant alternatif (AC) : liaison onduleur ? tableau électrique.
* Poser et câbler le smart meter.
* Conduire la mise en service complète de l'installation photovoltaïque, dans les règles de l'art.
* Activer et paramétrer la gestion par IA de l'installation (application de pilotage).
* Intervenir en autonomie sur les chantiers neuchâtelois et vaudois, selon le planning fixé avec le responsable électricien.
* Signaler au responsable électricien tout blocage technique ou non\-conformité qui dépasse votre périmètre.
Votre profil
**Obligatoire**
* CFC d’électricien.
* Envie de développer vos compétences en photovoltaïque et de gagner en autonomie, du raccordement à la mise en service.
* Goût du travail propre, soigné et conforme aux normes.
* Domicile dans le canton de Neuchâtel ou de Vaud, ou à proximité, les chantiers étant répartis entre ces deux cantons.
* Autorisation de travailler en Suisse.
* Permis de conduire indispensable pour les déplacements entre les chantiers.
* Français courant.
**Atouts**
* Expérience en photovoltaïque : onduleurs, smart meter, batteries.
* Aisance avec les outils numériques de paramétrage.
Ce que nous offrons
* Véhicule de service et outillage fournis.
* Un poste de terrain autonome, entre Neuchâtel et Vaud, sur des installations solaires neuves.
* Un secteur AC en construction, avec plusieurs postes prévus : vous en êtes parmi les premiers.
* Un responsable électricien joignable : votre référent technique est votre premier appui quand un chantier bloque.
* La responsabilité OIBT est portée par notre responsable technique : vous vous concentrez sur votre métier.
* Un travail utile : chaque mise en service, c'est un foyer de plus qui produit sa propre énergie.
* Salaire selon la CCT de la branche suisse de l'électricité.
